summary: Gmail setup is hard: registration is self-serve, but almost every useful Gmail scope is restricted and needs Google verification plus a third-party security assessment if data touches a server. Until verification passes, the app is limited to 100 test users with authorizations that expire after 7 days.
timeToProduction: 6–12 weeks for restricted scopes (Google's FAQ estimates 6 weeks for restricted verification, 2–3 business days for brand verification first)
effort: 3–5 days of work, plus security assessment remediation
cost: Google charges nothing; the security assessment is paid directly to a third-party assessor, at a price agreed with the assessor.

gates.title: Any Google Account can register an app
Testing mode caps you at 100 test users and 7-day authorizations
gates.what: In Testing status, projects are limited to 100 test users and authorizations expire after seven days.
gates.where: Google Cloud Console > Google Auth Platform > Audience (developer adds test users)
gates.todo: Add your own and testers' accounts as test users for development. Publish and verify before real users connect.

gates.title: Sensitive and restricted Gmail scopes require Google verification
gates.what: Apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes must complete verification. Restricted scopes also need a security assessment if the app accesses data through a third-party server.
gates.where: Google Cloud Console > Google Auth Platform > Branding, then Verification Center (developer submits)
gates.todo: Complete brand verification, then submit data access verification with a demo video. Prefer gmail.send (sensitive) over restricted scopes where it fits, since it avoids the security assessment.

gates.title: Google Workspace admins can block or restrict your app
gates.what: If an app requests a restricted service and the admin hasn't trusted it, users can't add it. Verification does not override admin settings.
gates.where: Google Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls (end user's Workspace admin acts)
gates.todo: Ask Workspace customers' admins to mark your app Trusted.

gates.title: No paid tier mentioned for Gmail API use
Annual reverification and security assessment
gates.what: Restricted apps must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months.
gates.where: Google emails the owner when recertification is due
gates.todo: Keep contact emails current so the reminder reaches you.

requirements.text: A Google Account to create a Google Cloud project
A publicly accessible app home page on a domain you own
A privacy policy on the same domain as the home page, linked on the consent screen

steps.text: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API.
Set the audience user type to External.
steps.why: External is available to any Google Account.

steps.text: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes your features need.
steps.why: gmail.send is sensitive; readonly, modify, compose, and metadata are restricted and trigger a security assessment if data goes through a server.
steps.detail: Declare them on the Data Access page.

steps.text: Fill in branding: app name, logo, support email, home page and privacy policy URLs.
Create an OAuth client and add testers as test users.
steps.why: Testing status allows up to 100 listed test users.
steps.detail: Authorizations expire after 7 days in Testing.

steps.text: Click Verify Branding, then Publish branding once it shows Ready to publish.
Record a demo video of the OAuth grant and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.
steps.detail: Show the OAuth grant process in English.

steps.text: Wait for Google's verification review and answer any emails from Google.
steps.detail: FAQ estimate: 10 business days for sensitive scopes, 6 weeks for restricted; not guaranteed.

steps.text: If using restricted scopes with a server, complete the security assessment with an assessor.

blockers.problem: Test users must re-authorize every week.
blockers.fix: Expected in Testing mode; publish and verify to remove the 7-day expiry.

blockers.problem: SMTP-only sending uses the broad mail.google.com scope.
blockers.fix: Use gmail.send instead; the broad scope violates the minimum scope policy.

blockers.problem: Workspace users get blocked from authorizing.
blockers.fix: Ask their admin to mark the app Trusted in API controls.

couldNotVerify: Couldn't read https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials (page has almost no text (likely rendered by JavaScript)), so nothing from it is confirmed.

claims.statement: Verification times are estimated at 2-3 business days for brand, 10 for sensitive scopes, 6 weeks for restricted scopes, not guaranteed.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: * Please note that these estimates are not guaranteed and will vary based on developer responsiveness
claims.note: Table lists 6 weeks for restricted scope verification.

claims.statement: Apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes must complete verification unless an exception applies.
claims.quote:
If your app requests
 sensitive 
or
 restricted 
scopes, you need to complete the verification process unless your app's use
qualifies for an exception .

claims.statement: In Testing status, projects are limited to 100 test users and authorizations expire after seven days.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.
claims.note: Same page states the 100 test user limit.

claims.statement: Apps with restricted data that can access it through a third-party server need a security assessment.
claims.quote:
If you store or transmit restricted scope data on servers, then you need to
complete a security assessment .

claims.statement: External projects are available to any user with a Google Account.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Projects configured with a user type of External are available to any user with a Google Account.

claims.statement: gmail.send is a sensitive scope; readonly, modify, compose, metadata are restricted.
claims.note: Classification from scope tables on the Gmail scopes page (Arabic); the FAQ also calls gmail.send sensitive.

claims.statement: If an app requests a restricted service and the admin hasn't trusted it, users can't add it.
claims.sourceTitle: Control which third-party & internal apps access Google Workspace data
claims.quote: While users are prompted to consent to apps, if an app requests access to a restricted service and you haven't specifically trusted the app, users can't add it.

claims.statement: Admins can block verified apps; verification does not override admin settings.
claims.note: Stated on the (Traditional Chinese) overview page: verified status does not override admin settings.

claims.statement: No paid tier requirement is mentioned on the Gmail quota page for standard use.
claims.sourceTitle: Limity wykorzystania | Gmail | Google for Developers
claims.note: Page says standard use has no extra charge, with overage fees planned later in 2026; absence claim.

claims.statement: Restricted apps must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months.
claims.quote:
As mentioned previously, to keep access to any verified restricted scopes, apps
must be reverified for compliance and complete a security assessment at least
every 12 months after your assessor's Letter of Assessment (LOA) approval date.

claims.statement: Google emails the owner when recertification is due.
claims.quote: The Google review team emails you when it is time to recertify your app.

claims.statement: Home page must be public and privacy policy hosted on the same domain and linked on the consent screen.
claims.quote:
Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your
site's logged-in users.

claims.statement: Google charges no fee; cost is agreed between developer and assessor.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Google does not charge the developer any fees for security assessment.

claims.statement: Compliant brand verification results are valid for 7 days before needing re-verification.
claims.quote: Note: Compliant verification results are valid for 7 days.

claims.statement: Demo video must show the OAuth grant process in English and be uploaded to YouTube as Unlisted.
claims.quote: Show the OAuth grant process that users will experience, in English.

claims.statement: SMTP-only sending with mail.google.com violates minimum scope policy; use gmail.send.
claims.sourceTitle: Frequently Asked Questions - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: If your app uses SMTP protocol only, note that using the broad access https://mail.google.com/ scope just for sending emails with the SMTP protocol violates the minimum scope policy .
